candidates: When guarding against absent or empty arrays before accessing array elements, avoid comparisons of the form `arr?.length < 1` or `arr?.length > 0`: when `arr` is `undefined` or `null`, optional chaining returns `undefined`, and relational comparisons with `undefined` produce `false` (NaN semantics), silently bypassing the guard and allowing element access to throw a TypeError. Use `!arr?.length` instead — it is correctly falsy for `undefined`, `null`, and zero-length arrays — or write an explicit `arr == null || arr.length === 0` check.
